articles.title: NVIDIA'S BOARD UNANIMOUSLY REINSTATES JENSEN HUANG AS CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia's board says Jensen Huang's candor and the input of US officials left them confident his return poses no national security risk, despite the pending independent director investigation into the foreign intelligence effort targeting him. The company is searching for a new Chief Compliance Officer, who will report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, alongside the independent National Security and Export Control Committee formed last week.

articles.title: TESLA AND SPACEX REPORTEDLY AIM TO SIGN AN ALL-STOCK MERGER BY YEAR-END, CREATING A ROUGHLY $3.5 TRILLION COMPANY
articles.summary: The FT says talks are moving toward a December 31 target, just before a new Congress where Democrats have vowed to probe Musk's companies, even though people familiar say an agreement isn't close. It would need more than 50% of all outstanding Tesla votes, where Musk holds about 20% of voting power, while he controls about 84% of SpaceX. Regulators in the US, China, Europe, and the UK could scrutinize it.

articles.title: ARIANE 64 LAUNCHES 36 AMAZON LEO SATELLITES TO ABOUT 460 KM ON ITS SECOND FLIGHT WITH LONGER P160C BOOSTERS, ARIANE 6'S 10TH STRAIGHT SUCCESS
articles.summary: The mission ran 2 hours and 4 minutes from liftoff to final satellite separation, bringing Arianespace's total to 136 Amazon Leo satellites this year. Amazon has ordered six more Ariane 64 launches, for 24 contracted overall.

articles.title: UBER AND NURO BEGIN DRIVERLESS TESTING OF LUCID GRAVITY ROBOTAXIS IN THE BAY AREA AHEAD OF A Q1 2027 COMMERCIAL LAUNCH
articles.summary: The Gravity robotaxi uses high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar, and radar running Nuro's driver, and testing has moved to no human at the wheel more than six months after California issued the driverless permit. Lucid is starting to build the first production versions at its Arizona factory, expanding the combined test fleet that stood at 100 vehicles earlier this year. Uber will own and operate the fleet and has committed to at least 20,000 Gravity SUVs over six years.

articles.title: PSIQUANTUM CEO VICTOR PENG SAYS QUANTUM IS A NEW FORM OF COMPUTING THAT WILL CREATE WHOLE NEW INDUSTRIES, WHILE GOVERNMENTS ARE STILL CATCHING UP
articles.summary: Peng became CEO in February, more than a year after the Australian federal and Queensland governments signed an AU$900 million deal with PsiQuantum to build a first-of-its-kind quantum computer near Brisbane. He echoes co-founder Mark Thompson's claim that quantum will dwarf AI in impact, and says many in government find that hard to grasp, though some parts have physicists and deeply technical staff.

articles.title: INSECT-SIZE FLYING ROBOTS COULD LEAVE THE LAB WITHIN TWO YEARS, BUT ONBOARD POWER, SENSING, AND CONTROL ARE THE BOTTLENECK
articles.summary: University of Washington's Sawyer Fuller predicts a fully autonomous insect-size flyer could fly free soon, though techniques from larger drones break down at this scale and onboard controllers and sensors add weight. MIT's wing-halved design hovered for about 1,000 seconds, 100 times longer than prior bots, and leaves room for batteries and sensors. Other designs, like FVW-Fly, control altitude but still lack directional control.

articles.title: LLMS HANDLE VERILOG BUT NOT LAYOUTS OR WAVEFORMS, AND AGENTS MULTIPLY LOAD ON DESIGN DATA SYSTEMS BY 10 TO 20X
articles.summary: Public RTL is plentiful, but models have never seen layouts, and a terabyte waveform database must be converted to text, burning tokens, so panelists want queryable abstractions. Each engineer directing 10 to 20 agents scales version control, NFS, and license demand the same way, and IP governance is a worry. Customers are drifting back from air-gapped open models toward frontier ones, while hybrid specialized models may handle things like temporal assertions.

articles.title: BAMBU LAB'S P3C BRINGS A SEVEN-TOOL CHANGER TO A $1,149 PRINTER, ABOUT HALF THE PRICE OF THE H3C
articles.summary: Instead of purging one nozzle on every color change, the Swaptek system swaps between separate nozzles in about six seconds, with five 0.4 mm tools included and two open slots that cost $99 each to fill. The build volume is 256 x 256 x 260 mm versus 330 x 320 x 325 mm on the H3C, and the bundled AMS 3P loads filament manually, which is the main compromise. It went on sale on November 24, with the seven-tool kit at $1,299.

articles.title: NVIDIA'S SSD WRITING BUG NEEDS ANOTHER HOTFIX AS ISSUE RETURNS
articles.summary: NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 40 series experiences ongoing excessive SSD writing, despite the recent GeForce Hotfix 621.35 reducing peak rates.
